description: `security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm` is ignored so that every datasource that reports release timestamps waits the same one day.

One day is what the repositories set for their package managers: `minimumReleaseAge: 1440` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (read by aube and by the pnpm that Renovate runs), `exclude-newer = "1 day"` for uv and `minimum_release_age = "1d"` for mise. A shorter window here would propose versions their resolvers decline to take, leaving lockfiles that a frozen install then rejects.
Raising it for npm alone would not buy protection either, since a local `aube add` still resolves at one day. Raise the package managers together with this if it ever needs to be stricter.

With `timestamp-optional`, an update that carries no release timestamp is proposed without waiting. The Docker datasource takes timestamps only from Docker Hub, so updates to images on other registries are not delayed, and neither are `pin` updates.

Turns off the weekly refresh that `config:best-practices` enables through `:maintainLockFilesWeekly`. Transitive dependencies move only with the direct ones that need them, and a daily scheduled validate run catches advisories through each repository's audit (uv audit, aube audit, govulncheck).

Renovate regenerates whole lockfiles with its own toolchain: it has no aube support and writes `pnpm-lock.yaml` with pnpm, and a refresh of `mise.lock` under another mise version dropped the tools that the shared mise-tasks declare.

description: Read Biome's version out of its tag names.

The mise manager's aqua backend does not consult the aqua registry, so it queries `github-tags` with a fixed `^v?(?<version>.+)` regardless of how the upstream tags its releases. Biome tags releases as `@biomejs/biome@X.Y.Z`, which that regex carries through whole, leaving nothing that parses as a version and no update ever proposed.
The trailing anchor keeps the sibling `@biomejs/js-api@` and the retired `cli/v` tags out.
